identity_reason: a visually hidden wrapper has no look of its own to derive; it only removes its content from the sight and keeps it for assistive tech, so there is nothing to render in three candidates
concept: VisuallyHidden keeps a name on the case that only a screen reader prints, the way a model number sits on the back plate: present for whoever needs it, absent from the face. The focusable form is the skip key that appears when the keyboard lands on it.

default_to_avoid.pattern: VisuallyHidden as display:none or an off-screen box at left:-9999px with a floating dark pill when the skip link is focused
default_to_avoid.why_not: display:none removes the words from assistive tech, an off-screen box scrolls the page sideways in right-to-left, and a floating pill is a second look the unit does not have.

references.source: Braun T 1000 world receiver (Dieter Rams, 1963): the model name and band names are printed on the case, never repeated on the face
system/FORM.md: a label names its control, and the model name is never the only identifier
WCAG 2.2 technique C7 and 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks: hide visually, keep in the accessibility tree; a skip link becomes visible when focused

derivation.consequence: labels name their control through aria-labelledby
derivation.form: The hidden text stays in the accessibility tree, so it can name a control that has no printed label and be pointed at by aria-labelledby.

derivation.consequence: fixed positions, so a unit's layout does not reflow between states
derivation.form: The hidden box leaves the flow and takes one pixel, and the revealed form is fixed to the viewport corner, so no neighbour moves when focus arrives.

derivation.consequence: no entry choreography, no idle animation; transitions only on state
derivation.form: The skip key appears at once on focus and disappears at once on blur, with no slide and no fade.

derivation.consequence: every part keeps ≥44px hit area even when it draws smaller
derivation.form: The revealed skip key is at least the 44px control height, so a person who tabs to it and then clicks has a full target.

derivation.consequence: orange appears once per unit, on the primary control's body only
derivation.form: The revealed key is raised plastic with primary ink and never orange, because a skip key is not the unit's one primary control.

variants.reason: VisuallyHidden is a behaviour wrapper with no form of its own, so no candidates were rendered; the focusable reveal reuses the raised part material and the system focus ring.

root.why: The wrapper clips its words to one pixel and takes them out of the flow, so they are read aloud and never seen.

data-focusable.why: A focusable wrapper holds a link or button that must be reachable by keyboard, so on focus it turns into a visible 44px raised key at the start corner.

focus.why: When the hidden element is itself the focusable link, keyboard focus on it brings the same raised key into view at once.

focus-within.why: The reveal is fixed to the viewport corner above the page, so showing it never pushes the content below it.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the revealed key takes a real border in the system text colour, so it stays visible when shadows and fills are dropped.
